title: Metals and Non-Metals: Properties, Reactivity, and Metallurgy

questions.question: The non-metal that conducts electricity is:
questions.rationale: Graphite's delocalized electrons carry current — the classic non-metal conductor among otherwise insulating non-metals.

questions.question: Which is the most reactive metal in this list?
questions.rationale: The reactivity series runs K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > H > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au — potassium is near the top.

questions.question: Which metal will NOT liberate hydrogen from dilute HCl?
questions.rationale: Copper sits below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace H⁺ from the acid.

questions.question: Roasting differs from calcination because roasting converts:
options: carbonates to oxides in limited air
sulphides to oxides in excess air
questions.rationale: Roasting heats sulphide ores in excess air (2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂); calcination heats carbonates in limited air.

questions.question: In the thermite reaction (Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → 2Fe + Al₂O₃), aluminium acts as a:
questions.rationale: Reactive aluminium strips oxygen from iron oxide — it reduces Fe₂O₃ while being oxidized itself.

questions.question: Brass is an alloy of:
questions.rationale: Brass = copper + zinc. Bronze is copper + tin; solder is lead + tin; stainless steel is iron + chromium + nickel.

questions.question: Which oxide is amphoteric?
questions.rationale: Al₂O₃ (like ZnO) reacts with both strong acids and strong bases; CO₂ and SO₂ are acidic, CaO basic.

questions.question: Froth flotation is used to concentrate:
questions.rationale: The process floats sulphide particles on rising bubbles while worthless gangue sinks and is drained off.

questions.question: Stainless steel resists rusting because it contains:
options: chromium and nickel alloyed into the iron
questions.rationale: Alloying iron with chromium (plus nickel) produces a protective, non-rusting alloy used for cutlery.

questions.question: The metal that is liquid at room temperature is:
questions.rationale: Mercury is the only metal liquid under everyday conditions; gallium only melts at 29.8 °C — in your hand.
